title: Why Do Wheels Spin Backwards on Camera? #camera
description:
A camera takes still pictures, often 30 a second. When each spoke moves more than half the gap to the next one between pictures, the shortest match is backwards, and that's what you see.

Full video: Why do wheels spin backwards on camera? → https://youtu.be/SxjS9sdc_Ek

subtitles: Why do wheels spin backwards on camera?
Its wheels spin backwards, slow down, and freeze.
A camera doesn't film smooth motion.
It takes still pictures, often 30 a second.
Your brain joins them up by picking the shortest move between them.
Spin a wheel slowly, and each spoke moves a little.
Faster, and each spoke lands just short of where the next one was.
The shortest match is now a small step backwards.
Land exactly on the next spoke, and the wheel seems to freeze.
